name: PR and media agencies

problems.words: Our media list is out of date and journalists keep changing outlets
quick_ideas: Check your top outlets once and update roles and beats, so pitches reach the right desk
Mark when each entry was last confirmed, so stale ones stand out.

workzap_build.text: an agency-owned media register with outlet, role, beat and last contact, prompting the team to refresh entries that haven't been confirmed recently.

problems.free_stops: the register structure and refresh routine are set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many outlet contacts changed role since your last big pitch, so you see how much of the list is already drifting.
Give one person a fixed weekly slot to note outlet and beat changes in one master list, so pitches stop going to old desks.

problems.words: Each account manager keeps their own contacts, and they leave with them
quick_ideas: Ask each AM to add their working outlet contacts to the shared list, so the agency holds the relationships
Note who owns each relationship, so handovers are possible.

workzap_build.text: the shared media register with access controls and a log of every pitch and contact, so relationships stay with the agency.

problems.free_stops: access rights and what is logged are worked out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare one account manager's contact notes with the agency list once, so you see how much relationship information would walk out.
Make one shared contact notebook the handover place for every account, so client outreach survives staff changes.

problems.words: We spend days compiling coverage reports
quick_ideas: Start logging coverage the day it appears, so month-end isn't a hunt
Agree one report layout for all clients, so nobody rebuilds it.

workzap_build.text: a coverage log with links, screenshots and outlet type that builds each client's monthly report automatically.

problems.free_stops: the report layout and how coverage is captured are kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note how many coverage items are gathered after month end for one client, so you see why reporting days get swallowed.
Give one person the daily job of writing new coverage into one running client log, so report building becomes a tidy wrap up.

problems.words: Coverage gets mixed up between clients in our records
quick_ideas: Tag every clipping with its client when it's saved, so it can't land in the wrong report
Check last month's reports once for mix-ups, so you know the scale.

workzap_build.text: a pitch and coverage tracker per client, so each clipping is tied to the story and client it came from.

problems.free_stops: how pitches link to coverage is designed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Check one recent client's coverage file against its report once, so you can count how often items sit under the wrong name.
Choose one place where every coverage item is written with the client name at saving time, so reports stop mixing accounts.

problems.words: Press releases go through six rounds of client approval and news goes stale
quick_ideas: Ask each client to name one approver, so drafts stop circulating
Put an approve-by time on every release, so delays are visible.

workzap_build.text: an approval workflow for releases with timestamps and automatic client nudges as the deadline nears.

problems.free_stops: the approval steps and nudge timings are set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many client comments arrive after the internal draft is ready for one release, so the approval drag becomes visible.
Assign one client side approver contact for each release in one shared note, so drafts stop circling through extra people.

problems.words: We pay outlets for ads and the client pays us months later
quick_ideas: List every booking you've paid for but not yet billed or collected, so the gap is clear
Chase the oldest one this week, so money starts moving.

workzap_build.text: a media-buying ledger per client with bookings, outlet invoices, client billing and payment status.

problems.free_stops: how bookings flow into client billing is kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count bookings already placed where the client approval note is missing or scattered, so delayed handoffs tying up work become visible.
Give one staff member a daily slot to note every placed booking awaiting client follow-up in one notebook, so chasing stops slipping.

problems.words: Retainer clients expect unlimited events and crisis support
quick_ideas: Write down once what each retainer includes, so extras are recognisable
List the extras delivered last quarter for one client, so you have facts for the renewal talk.

workzap_build.text: a retainer scope tracker comparing agreed activities against delivered work each month.

problems.free_stops: how activities are logged and compared is worked out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note every extra event and urgent support request for one retainer client this month, so renewal talks rest on actual workload.
Assign one person to keep one running extras list for each retainer, so added work is noticed while it is happening.

problems.words: Event suppliers deliver late and budgets overrun
quick_ideas: Put the next event's suppliers, deliverables and deadlines on one sheet, so slips show early
Compare budget and actuals once for the last event, so you see where it ran over.

workzap_build.text: an event planner with supplier deliverables, deadlines and budget versus actual updated as costs come in.

problems.free_stops: the event stages and budget tracking are designed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare the last event brief with what suppliers actually delivered late or differently, so the repeat causes of overruns stand out.
Give one person the job of keeping all supplier promises and delivery times in one notebook, so delays get spotted before event day.

problems.words: Weekend crises land on me personally, there's no rota
quick_ideas: Draw up one out-of-hours rota for the next month, so cover is shared
Agree who the rota person calls next, so escalation is clear.

workzap_build.text: an out-of-hours rota with the escalation chain and reminders to whoever is on duty.

problems.free_stops: rota rules and the escalation chain are set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many weekend client issues came straight to you in the last month, so the true out of hours load is clear.
Name one duty person for each upcoming weekend and write the handover note in one place, so cover no longer rests on you alone.

problems.words: Products we send to influencers and media aren't tracked
quick_ideas: List every product sent out this month with recipient type and date, so you know what is out
Mark which ones have had a follow-up, so nothing is forgotten.

workzap_build.text: a seeding tracker showing products sent, follow-up dates and whether coverage came back.

problems.free_stops: the follow-up rules are kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count the product samples sent out this week by client and recipient type, so missing returns and follow ups are easier to spot.
Give one staff member the send out notebook and require every parcel to be written there, so nothing leaves without a record.

never_say: Any legal, defamation, regulatory or crisis-response advice.
That a story will get coverage or that PR will deliver a measurable result.
Anything involving fake news, smear campaigns, fake reviews, undisclosed paid coverage where unlawful, or bribing officials.
Requests for journalists' personal numbers, client confidential plans or unannounced news.
If a crisis involves danger to people, point to emergency services first.

sample_reply.person: We lose the first week of every month just compiling coverage reports. Is there a better way?
sample_reply.pi: Yes, there is, and you can start this week. 1) Log each piece of coverage the day it appears, tagged with its client, so month-end stops being a hunt. 2) Agree one report layout for every client, so nobody rebuilds it from scratch. Workzap can do this automatically for you: a coverage log that builds each client's monthly report on its own. Would you like me to put together a solution document and quote for you? You're free to say no.
